name: Israel asking for a king
charge: Rejecting the Lord's rule to be like the nations
summary: The elders came to Samuel and demanded a king to judge them like all the nations. The Lord told Samuel: they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me. Warned what a king would take from them, they said, nay, but we will have a king over us.
offense: Israel's elders named Samuel's age and his sons' corruption, then demanded a king to judge them like the nations (1 Samuel 8:4-5). The law had already provided for a king whom the Lord would choose, a brother who would remain under the commandments (Deuteronomy 17:14-20). The offense was not the existence of every king. It was the rejection of the Lord's reign in favour of the security Israel imagined the nations possessed. Samuel prayed, and the Lord told him that the people had rejected him, not merely his prophet. Their request continued the course of forsaking him and serving other gods since Egypt (1 Samuel 8:6-9). Joshua's congregation had promised to serve the Lord and obey his voice (Joshua 24:21-24). Now the people insisted upon a visible ruler to go before them and fight their battles, though the Lord had repeatedly delivered them through the judges (1 Samuel 8:19-20; 12:6-12).
judgment: The Lord granted the request and sent thunder and rain in wheat harvest as a sign of his displeasure. The people feared and confessed, and Samuel answered, fear not; ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord. They got Saul.

entries.commentary: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel: Joel the firstborn and Abiah his second, judges in Beersheba. But his sons walked not in his ways; they turned aside after lucre, took bribes, and perverted judgment.

All the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel unto Ramah: thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways; now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a king like the other nations have. Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

The thing displeased Samuel when they said, Give us a king to judge us, and Samuel prayed unto the Lord. The Lord said, Hearken unto the voice of the people, for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them; according to all the works they have done since the day I brought them up out of Egypt, forsaking me and serving other gods, so do they also unto thee. Just as they rejected the Most High, they were rejecting Samuel and his counsel. Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

Samuel told all the words of the Lord unto the people that asked of him a king: this will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you. He will take your sons for his chariots and to be his horsemen; he will appoint him captains over thousands and captains over fifties, and set them to ear his ground, to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war. He will take your daughters to be confectionaries, cooks, and bakers; your fields, your vineyards, and your oliveyards, even the best of them, and give them to his servants; the tenth of your seed and of your vineyards for his officers; your menservants, your maidservants, your goodliest young men, and your asses to his work; the tenth of your sheep: and ye shall be his servants. And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you, and the Lord will not hear you in that day. The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay, but we will have a king over us, that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles. Samuel heard all the words of the people and rehearsed them in the ears of the Lord, and the Lord said, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king; and Samuel sent every man unto his city.
Samuel took a vial of oil and poured it upon Saul's head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the Lord hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?

Samuel gave Saul the signs that would confirm the word: two men by Rachel's sepulchre saying the asses are found and thy father sorroweth for you; three men at the plain of Tabor going up to God to Bethel, who would give him two loaves of bread; and at the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is, a company of prophets coming down from the high place, and the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man. When these signs are come unto thee, do as occasion serve thee, for God is with thee; and go down before me to Gilgal, and seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee and shew thee what thou shalt do.
When Saul had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart, and all those signs came to pass that day.

When they came to the hill, the company of prophets met him, and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied among them. The people that knew him beforetime said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? and it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets?
Saul's uncle asked him where they went and what Samuel said unto them. Saul told him plainly that the asses were found, but of the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not.

Samuel called the people together unto the Lord to Mizpeh: thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all kingdoms, and of them that oppressed you. Remember, we just came out of reading Judges, and we were oppressed by many nations there. Every time one of our judges rose up and delivered us from oppression, we would get right during the life of that judge, and when that judge died we went right back into our falling. And ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you out of all your adversities and your tribulations; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us.

When all the tribes came near, the tribe of Benjamin was taken, then the family of Matri, and Saul the son of Kish was taken; and when they sought him he could not be found, for the Lord answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff. They ran and fetched him thence, and when he stood among the people he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward; he was real tall, taller than everybody. Samuel said unto all the people, See ye him whom the Lord hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people; and all the people shouted, and said, God save the king.
Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the Lord; and Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.

Saul went home to Gibeah, and there went with him a band of men whose hearts God had touched. But the children of Belial said, How shall this man save us? and they despised him, and brought him no presents; but he held his peace. That is just like us today. When a man gets raised up, instead of brothers being happy for him, a brother may feel that should have been me, not knowing he has things to work on in his own spirit, and not realizing that with rank comes responsibility; you should already be doing the work. Men are being raised up for order's sake in Israel, to help set the nation in order, and we should bless them. That is why the scriptures call the ones who despised him the children of Belial, the children of the devil: the haters.

At the end of chapter 11 Israel crowned Saul at Gilgal. Back in chapter 8 the people had pressured Samuel because they wanted to be like the nations round about them, and the Most High led him to choose Saul the son of Kish. This is the aftermath speech. Samuel is putting it on record: I hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me and made a king over you; whatever happens from here came from what you asked for.

Samuel establishes his blamelessness before he reasons with them. He walked before Israel from his childhood unto this day; whose ox or ass has he taken, whom has he defrauded or oppressed, from whose hand has he taken any bribe? Speak up now and he will restore it. The people answer that he has not defrauded nor oppressed them nor taken anything from any man's hand, and the Lord and his anointed are witness that day. Samuel was never a bad guy to the nation of Israel, and the whole congregation confirms it.

It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now stand still, that Samuel may reason with them before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord which he did to them and to their fathers.

When Jacob was come into Egypt and your fathers cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and made Israel dwell in this place. When they forgat the Lord he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and of the Philistines, and of the king of Moab; this is the history of the book of Judges, starting in chapter 4. They cried unto the Lord and confessed they had sinned in forsaking him and serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. That is the same lesson Samuel taught in chapter 7: when the Philistines beat Israel, they went and got the ark of the covenant, got beat even worse, and lost the ark. It is not just about having the ark of the covenant among you; you have to put away the idols and stop serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

When Nahash king of the children of Ammon came against them, Israel said, Nay, but a king shall reign over us, when the Lord their God was their king. That demand exposed their disbelief in the Lord; they wanted a king they could see and touch, because all the nations around them had kings. Now behold the king whom ye have chosen and whom ye have desired. If ye will fear the Lord and serve him and obey his voice and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God. If you and your king do not rebel against the voice of the Lord, the ultimate king, you will be all right. Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

Once the Lord thundered, the people acknowledged their folly: pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not, for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king. Now they confess they were dead wrong for asking for a king.

Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy.

Turn ye not aside, for then should ye go after vain things which cannot profit nor deliver, for they are vain. Something you make with your own hands is not going to make thunder and rain come on your harvest day to show you how wicked you are; idols cannot help you or save you. Our people do the same thing today, icing out crosses and things of that nature that cannot do a thing for them; those are the vain things our people follow after. Samuel warned Israel not to do it, and over a span of time that is exactly what they ended up doing.

The Lord will not forsake his people for his great name's sake, because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people. That is part of the comfort of the scriptures: he may purge his people, but he will never exterminate the Israelites, for his name's sake. Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said.

Marinate on this verse. God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you; but I will teach you the good and the right way. Samuel says that as a leader who loved his nation, if he stopped praying for them, that itself would put him in sin. For those who battle with prayer, meditate on that: ceasing to pray for your nation puts you in sin.

Only fear the Lord and serve him in truth with all your heart, and consider how great things he hath done for you. But if ye shall still do wickedly, after the speech, the warning, and the thunder, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king. That is what [Deuteronomy 28:36](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v36) said: you and the king you set over you will be brought into subjection to the other nations. Samuel's exhortation was to get their minds on the right track: you asked for the wrong thing, but now that you have it, keep the commandments and you will be all right.
When Ephraim spake trembling, he exalted himself in Israel, but when he offended in Baal, he died.

Now they sin more and more and have made them molten images of their silver, idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen; they say of them, Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves. Remember the time frame and the other prophets that were prophesying during that time; the craftsman was making idols in the images of men. -
Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud, as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.
Yet the Most High is the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no god but him, for there is no saviour beside him.

He knew them in the wilderness, in the land of great drought. According to their pasture they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore they forgot him. That is what happens to us; when we get all the things we need, our food, water, and clothing, and a little excess, we forget the Lord.

Therefore he will be unto them as a lion, as a leopard by the way will he observe them; he will meet them as a bear bereaved of her whelps, rend the caul of their heart, and there devour them like a lion; the wild beast shall tear them.
O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself, but in the Most High is thine help.

He will be thy king; where is any other that may save thee in all thy cities, and thy judges of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes? The Lord is telling us there is none that saveth but him. -
He gave thee a king in his anger and took him away in his wrath.

The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up, his sin is hid. The sorrows of a travailing woman shall come upon him; he is an unwise son, for he should not stay long in the place of the breaking forth of children.
The Most High will ransom them from the power of the grave and redeem them from death; O death, he will be thy plagues; O grave, he will be thy destruction; repentance shall be hid from his eyes.

Though he be fruitful among his brethren, an east wind shall come, the wind of the Lord coming up from the wilderness, and his spring shall become dry and his fountain dried up; he shall spoil the treasure of all pleasant vessels.

Samaria shall become desolate, for she hath rebelled against her God; they shall fall by the sword, their infants dashed in pieces, and their women with child ripped up. This was a future prophecy at the time Hosea prophesied, about Assyria coming into the land. -

Thou shalt not sacrifice unto the Most High any bullock or sheep wherein is blemish, or any evilfavouredness, for that is an abomination unto the Lord thy God. Back then you could be put to death for sacrificing a bullock or sheep with a blemish, because doing an abominable thing carried death.

If there be found among you man or woman that hath wrought wickedness, transgressed the covenant, and gone and served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, which the Most High commanded not, the matter had to be established first. A lot of people do not know how to apply [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1); the precept for [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is [Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4). Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain that such abomination is wrought in Israel, then judgment proceeds. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death. The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. Wait till we go back to this: the ones who witnessed against you were the first to lay hands on you, so a false witness could not hide behind the crowd. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.

If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, matters of controversy within thy gates, then thou shalt get thee up into the place which the Lord shall choose. Come unto the priests the Levites and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment; thou shalt do according to all that they inform thee, according to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. The man that will do presumptuously and will not hearken unto the priest that standeth to minister before the Most High, or unto the judge, even that man shall die; and all the people shall hear, and fear, and do no more presumptuously.

When thou art come unto the land and shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations that are about me, thou shalt in any wise set him king whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother. These are the laws for a king that is to rule over Israel. He shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt to multiply horses, for the Lord hath said, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way. Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away. You hear a lot of these dudes today saying king this and king that, and many of the same men pushing for multiple wives; the law of the king says do not multiply wives to thyself. Neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

When he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites. It shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Most High and keep all the words of this law and these statutes to do them. The purpose: that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, that he turn not aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, and that he prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children, in the midst of Israel.

verses.text: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together, and came to Samuel unto Ramah,
And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.
But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the Lord.
And the Lord said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.

According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, wherewith they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also unto thee.
Now therefore hearken unto their voice: howbeit yet protest solemnly unto them, and shew them the manner of the king that shall reign over them.

And he said, This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and some shall run before his chariots.

And he will appoint him captains over thousands, and captains over fifties; and will set them to ear his ground, and to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war, and instruments of his chariots.
And he will take your daughters to be confectionaries, and to be cooks, and to be bakers.
And he will take your fields, and your vineyards, and your oliveyards, even the best of them, and give them to his servants.
And he will take the tenth of your seed, and of your vineyards, and give to his officers, and to his servants.
And he will take your menservants, and your maidservants, and your goodliest young men, and your asses, and put them to his work.
He will take the tenth of your sheep: and ye shall be his servants.
And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you; and the Lord will not hear you in that day.
Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay; but we will have a king over us;
That we also may be like all the nations; and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.

And ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you out of all your adversities and your tribulations; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us. Now therefore present yourselves before the Lord by your tribes, and by your thousands.
And when ye saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, ye said unto me, Nay; but a king shall reign over us: when the Lord your God was your king.
Now therefore behold the king whom ye have chosen, and whom ye have desired! and, behold, the Lord hath set a king over you.

Is it not wheat harvest to day? I will call unto the Lord, and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king.
So Samuel called unto the Lord; and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.
And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not: for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king.
And Samuel said unto the people, Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart;
I gave thee a king in mine anger, and took him away in my wrath.

When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me;

Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
